chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said:

I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'Descend into the grave with the turban and the cap on your head, and without the shoes and the pallium; and loosen your buttons, and by that the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) flowed.'

And let him seek Refuge with Allah from the Pelted Satan, and let him recite the Opening of the Book (Al-Fatiha), and the Two Protecting Chapters (Al-Mu'awwidhatayn), and 'Say: He is Allah, One' (Al-Ikhlas), and the Verse of the Throne (Ayat Al-Kursi).

And if he is able to bare his cheek and place it on the ground, let him do so; and let him testify (the Shahadah) and let him mention (Allah) whatever he knows until he ends up to his companion (the deceased).

key_terms.آيَةَ الْكُرْسِيِّ: The Verse of the Throne (Ayat Al-Kursi)
key_terms.الْمُعَوِّذَتَيْنِ: The Two Protecting Chapters (Al-Falaq and An-Nas)

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended rituals and recitations when entering the grave for the deceased?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific Sunnah for the deceased entering the grave, emphasizing modest attire (turban and cap, excluding shoes and pallium) and spiritual preparation through recitation of key Quranic chapters and verses. It highlights the practical act of lying on the side with the cheek against the earth, a posture symbolizing humility and readiness for the individual reckoning, while the deceased recites the Shahada and Dhikr until the attendants depart.
